metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: How lonely lies the city, once so full of people! She who was great among the nations has become a widow. The princess of the provinces has become a slave.
units.rightText: How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people! She is become as a widow, that was great among the nations! She that was a princess among the provinces is become tributary!
leftNotes: 1:1 This chapter is an acrostic poem, each verse beginning with the successive letters of the Hebrew alphabet.

units.leftText: She weeps aloud in the night, with tears upon her cheeks. Among all her lovers there is no one to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.
units.rightText: She weepeth sore in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks; Among all her lovers she hath none to comfort her: All her friends have dealt treacherously with her; they are become her enemies.

units.leftText: Judah has gone into exile under affliction and harsh slavery; she dwells among the nations but finds no place to rest. All her pursuers have overtaken her in the midst of her distress.
units.rightText: Judah is gone into captivity because of affliction, and because of great servitude; She dwelleth among the nations, she findeth no rest: All her persecutors overtook her within the straits.

units.leftText: The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to her appointed feasts. All her gates are deserted; her priests groan, her maidens grieve, and she herself is bitter with anguish.
units.rightText: The ways of Zion do mourn, because none come to the solemn assembly; All her gates are desolate, her priests do sigh: Her virgins are afflicted, and she herself is in bitterness.

units.leftText: Her foes have become her masters; her enemies are at ease. For the LORD has brought her grief because of her many transgressions. Her children have gone away as captives before the enemy.
units.rightText: Her adversaries are become the head, her enemies prosper; For Jehovah hath afflicted her for the multitude of her transgressions: Her young children are gone into captivity before the adversary.

units.leftText: All the splendor has departed from the Daughter of Zion. Her princes are like deer that find no pasture; they lack the strength to flee in the face of the hunter.
units.rightText: And from the daughter of Zion all her majesty is departed: Her princes are become like harts that find no pasture, And they are gone without strength before the pursuer.

units.leftText: In the days of her affliction and wandering Jerusalem remembers all the treasures that were hers in days of old. When her people fell into enemy hands she received no help. Her enemies looked upon her, laughing at her downfall.
units.rightText: Jerusalem remembereth in the days of her affliction and of her miseries all her pleasant things that were from the days of old: When her people fell into the hand of the adversary, and none did help her, The adversaries saw her, they did mock at her desolations.

units.leftText: Jerusalem has sinned greatly; therefore she has become an object of scorn. All who honored her now despise her, for they have seen her nakedness; she herself groans and turns away.
units.rightText: Jerusalem hath grievously sinned; therefore she is become as an unclean thing; All that honored her despise her, because they have seen her nakedness: Yea, she sigheth, and turneth backward.

units.leftText: Her uncleanness stains her skirts; she did not consider her end. Her downfall was astounding; there was no one to comfort her. Look, O LORD, on my affliction, for the enemy has triumphed!
units.rightText: Her filthiness was in her skirts; she remembered not her latter end; Therefore is she come down wonderfully; she hath no comforter: Behold, O Jehovah, my affliction; for the enemy hath magnified himself.

units.leftText: The adversary has seized all her treasures. For she has seen the nations enter her sanctuary— those You had forbidden to enter Your assembly.
units.rightText: The adversary hath spread out his hand upon all her pleasant things: For she hath seen that the nations are entered into her sanctuary, Concerning whom thou didst command that they should not enter into thine assembly.

units.leftText: All her people groan as they search for bread. They have traded their treasures for food to keep themselves alive. Look, O LORD, and consider, for I have become despised.
units.rightText: All her people sigh, they seek bread; They have given their pleasant things for food to refresh the soul: See, O Jehovah, and behold; for I am become abject.

units.leftText: Is this nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look around and see! Is there any sorrow like mine, which was inflicted on me, which the LORD made me suffer on the day of His fierce anger?
units.rightText: Is it nothing to you, all ye that pass by? Behold, and see if there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow, which is brought upon me, Wherewith Jehovah hath afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger.

units.leftText: He sent fire from on high, and it overpowered my bones. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He made me desolate, faint all the day long.
units.rightText: From on high hath he sent fire into my bones, and it prevaileth against them; He hath spread a net for my feet, he hath turned me back: He hath made me desolate and faint all the day.

units.leftText: My transgressions are bound into a yoke, knit together by His hand; they are draped over my neck, and the Lord has broken my strength. He has delivered me into the hands of those I cannot withstand.
units.rightText: The yoke of my transgressions is bound by his hand; They are knit together, they are come up upon my neck; he hath made my strength to fail: The Lord hath delivered me into their hands, against whom I am not able to stand.
leftNotes: 1:14 Most Hebrew manuscripts; other Hebrew manuscripts and LXX He kept watch over my sins

units.leftText: The Lord has rejected all the mighty men in my midst; He has summoned an army against me to crush my young warriors. Like grapes in a winepress, the Lord has trampled the Virgin Daughter of Judah.
units.rightText: The Lord hath set at nought all my mighty men in the midst of me; He hath called a solemn assembly against me to crush my young men: The Lord hath trodden as in a winepress the virgin daughter of Judah.
leftNotes: 1:15 Or has set a time for me

units.leftText: For these things I weep; my eyes flow with tears. For there is no one nearby to comfort me, no one to revive my soul. My children are destitute because the enemy has prevailed.
units.rightText: For these things I weep; mine eye, mine eye runneth down with water; Because the comforter that should refresh my soul is far from me: My children are desolate, because the enemy hath prevailed.

units.leftText: Zion stretches out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her. The LORD has decreed against Jacob that his neighbors become his foes. Jerusalem has become an unclean thing among them.
units.rightText: Zion spreadeth forth her hands; there is none to comfort her; Jehovah hath commanded concerning Jacob, that they that are round about him should be his adversaries: Jerusalem is among them as an unclean thing.

units.leftText: The LORD is righteous, yet I rebelled against His command. Listen, all you people; look upon my suffering. My young men and maidens have gone into captivity.
units.rightText: Jehovah is righteous; for I have rebelled against his commandment: Hear, I pray you, all ye peoples, and behold my sorrow: My virgins and my young men are gone into captivity.

units.leftText: I called out to my lovers, but they have betrayed me. My priests and elders perished in the city while they searched for food to keep themselves alive.
units.rightText: I called for my lovers, but they deceived me: My priests and mine elders gave up the ghost in the city, While they sought them food to refresh their souls.

units.leftText: See, O LORD, how distressed I am! I am churning within; my heart is pounding within me, for I have been most rebellious. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside, there is death.
units.rightText: Behold, O Jehovah; for I am in distress; my heart is troubled; My heart is turned within me; for I have grievously rebelled: Abroad the sword bereaveth, at home there is as death.

units.leftText: People have heard my groaning, but there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble; they are glad that You have caused it. May You bring the day You have announced, so that they may become like me.
units.rightText: They have heard that I sigh; there is none to comfort me; All mine enemies have heard of my trouble; they are glad that thou hast done it: Thou wilt bring the day that thou hast proclaimed, and they shall be like unto me.

units.leftText: Let all their wickedness come before You, and deal with them as You have dealt with me because of all my transgressions. For my groans are many, and my heart is faint.
units.rightText: Let all their wickedness come before thee; And do unto them, as thou hast done unto me for all my transgressions: For my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.

units.leftText: How the Lord has covered the Daughter of Zion with the cloud of His anger! He has cast the glory of Israel from heaven to earth. He has abandoned His footstool in the day of His anger.
units.rightText: How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger! He hath cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, And hath not remembered his footstool in the day of his anger.
leftNotes: 2:1 This chapter is an acrostic poem, each verse beginning with the successive letters of the Hebrew alphabet.

units.leftText: Without pity the Lord has swallowed up all the dwellings of Jacob. In His wrath He has demolished the fortified cities of the Daughter of Judah. He brought to the ground and defiled her kingdom and its princes.
units.rightText: The Lord hath swallowed up all the habitations of Jacob, and hath not pitied: He hath thrown down in his wrath the strongholds of the daughter of Judah; He hath brought them down to the ground; he hath profaned the kingdom and the princes thereof.

units.leftText: In fierce anger He has cut off every horn of Israel and withdrawn His right hand at the approach of the enemy. He has burned in Jacob like a flaming fire that consumes everything around it.
units.rightText: He hath cut off in fierce anger all the horn of Israel; He hath drawn back his right hand from before the enemy: And he hath burned up Jacob like a flaming fire, which devoureth round about.

units.leftText: He has bent His bow like an enemy; His right hand is positioned. Like a foe He has killed all who were pleasing to the eye; He has poured out His wrath like fire on the tent of the Daughter of Zion.
units.rightText: He hath bent his bow like an enemy, he hath stood with his right hand as an adversary, And hath slain all that were pleasant to the eye: In the tent of the daughter of Zion he hath poured out his wrath like fire.

units.leftText: The Lord is like an enemy; He has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces and destroyed her strongholds. He has multiplied mourning and lamentation for the Daughter of Judah.
units.rightText: The Lord is become as an enemy, he hath swallowed up Israel; He hath swallowed up all her palaces, he hath destroyed his strongholds; And he hath multiplied in the daughter of Judah mourning and lamentation.

units.leftText: He has laid waste His tabernacle like a garden booth; He has destroyed His place of meeting. The LORD has made Zion forget her appointed feasts and Sabbaths. In His fierce anger He has despised both king and priest.
units.rightText: And he hath violently taken away his tabernacle, as if it were of a garden; he hath destroyed his place of assembly: Jehovah hath caused solemn assembly and sabbath to be forgotten in Zion, And hath despised in the indignation of his anger the king and the priest.

units.leftText: The Lord has rejected His altar; He has abandoned His sanctuary; He has delivered the walls of her palaces into the hand of the enemy. They have raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on the day of an appointed feast.
units.rightText: The Lord hath cast off his altar, he hath abhorred his sanctuary; He hath given up into the hand of the enemy the walls of her palaces: They have made a noise in the house of Jehovah, as in the day of a solemn assembly.

units.leftText: The LORD determined to destroy the wall of the Daughter of Zion. He stretched out a measuring line and did not withdraw His hand from destroying. He made the ramparts and walls lament; together they waste away.
units.rightText: Jehovah hath purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion; He hath stretched out the line, he hath not withdrawn his hand from destroying; And he hath made the rampart and wall to lament; they languish together.

units.leftText: Her gates have sunk into the ground; He has destroyed and shattered their bars. Her king and her princes are exiled among the nations, the law is no more, and even her prophets find no vision from the LORD.
units.rightText: Her gates are sunk into the ground; he hath destroyed and broken her bars: Her king and her princes are among the nations where the law is not; Yea, her prophets find no vision from Jehovah.

units.leftText: The elders of the Daughter of Zion sit on the ground in silence. They have thrown dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.
units.rightText: The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, they keep silence; They have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth: The virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

units.leftText: My eyes fail from weeping; I am churning within. My heart is poured out in grief over the destruction of the daughter of my people, because children and infants faint in the streets of the city.
units.rightText: Mine eyes do fail with tears, my heart is troubled; My liver is poured upon the earth, because of the destruction of the daughter of my people, Because the young children and the sucklings swoon in the streets of the city.

units.leftText: They cry out to their mothers: “Where is the grain and wine?” as they faint like the wounded in the streets of the city, as their lives fade away in the arms of their mothers.
units.rightText: They say to their mothers, Where is grain and wine? When they swoon as the wounded in the streets of the city, When their soul is poured out into their mothers’ bosom.

units.leftText: What can I say for you? To what can I compare you, O Daughter of Jerusalem? To what can I liken you, that I may console you, O Virgin Daughter of Zion? For your wound is as deep as the sea. Who can ever heal you?
units.rightText: What shall I testify unto thee? what shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? What shall I compare to thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? For thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee?

units.leftText: The visions of your prophets were empty and deceptive; they did not expose your guilt to ward off your captivity. The burdens they envisioned for you were empty and misleading.
units.rightText: Thy prophets have seen for thee false and foolish visions; And they have not uncovered thine iniquity, to bring back thy captivity, But have seen for thee false oracles and causes of banishment.

units.leftText: All who pass by clap their hands at you in scorn. They hiss and shake their heads at the Daughter of Jerusalem: “Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?”
units.rightText: All that pass by clap their hands at thee; They hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, Is this the city that men called The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?

units.leftText: All your enemies open their mouths against you. They hiss and gnash their teeth, saying, “We have swallowed her up. This is the day for which we have waited. We have lived to see it!”
units.rightText: All thine enemies have opened their mouth wide against thee; They hiss and gnash the teeth; they say, We have swallowed her up; Certainly this is the day that we looked for; we have found, we have seen it.

units.leftText: The LORD has done what He planned; He has accomplished His decree, which He ordained in days of old; He has overthrown you without pity. He has let the enemy gloat over you and exalted the horn of your foes.
units.rightText: Jehovah hath done that which he purposed; he hath fulfilled his word that he commanded in the days of old; He hath thrown down, and hath not pitied: And he hath caused the enemy to rejoice over thee; he hath exalted the horn of thine adversaries.

units.leftText: The hearts of the people cry out to the Lord. O wall of the Daughter of Zion, let your tears run down like a river day and night. Give yourself no relief, and your eyes no rest.
units.rightText: Their heart cried unto the Lord: O wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears run down like a river day and night; Give thyself no respite; let not the apple of thine eye cease.
leftNotes: 2:18 Literally Their heart cries out to the Lord.

units.leftText: Arise, cry out in the night from the first watch of the night. Pour out your heart like water in the presence of the Lord. Lift up your hands to Him for the lives of your children who are fainting from hunger on the corner of every street.
units.rightText: Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches; Pour out thy heart like water before the face of the Lord: Lift up thy hands toward him for the life of thy young children, that faint for hunger at the head of every street.
leftNotes: 2:19 That is, between six and nine at night

units.leftText: Look, O LORD, and consider: Whom have You ever treated like this? Should women eat their offspring, the infants they have nurtured? Should priests and prophets be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
units.rightText: See, O Jehovah, and behold to whom thou hast done thus! Shall the women eat their fruit, the children that are dandled in the hands? Shall the priest and the prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the Lord?

units.leftText: Both young and old lie together in the dust of the streets. My young men and maidens have fallen by the sword. You have slain them in the day of Your anger; You have slaughtered them without compassion.
units.rightText: The youth and the old man lie on the ground in the streets; My virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword: Thou hast slain them in the day of thine anger; thou hast slaughtered, and not pitied.

units.leftText: You summoned my terrors on every side, as for the day of an appointed feast. In the day of the LORD’s anger no one escaped or survived; my enemy has destroyed those I nurtured and reared.
units.rightText: Thou hast called, as in the day of a solemn assembly, my terrors on every side; And there was none that escaped or remained in the day of Jehovah’s anger: Those that I have dandled and brought up hath mine enemy consumed.

units.leftText: I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of God’s wrath.
units.rightText: I am the man that hath seen affliction by the rod of his wrath.
leftNotes: 3:1 This chapter is an acrostic poem, each 3–verse stanza beginning with the successive letters of the Hebrew alphabet.

units.leftText: He has driven me away and made me walk in darkness instead of light.
units.rightText: He hath led me and caused me to walk in darkness, and not in light.

units.leftText: Indeed, He keeps turning His hand against me all day long.
units.rightText: Surely against me he turneth his hand again and again all the day.

units.leftText: He has worn away my flesh and skin; He has shattered my bones.
units.rightText: My flesh and my skin hath he made old; he hath broken my bones.

units.leftText: He has besieged me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.
units.rightText: He hath builded against me, and compassed me with gall and travail.

units.leftText: He has made me dwell in darkness like those dead for ages.
units.rightText: He hath made me to dwell in dark places, as those that have been long dead.

units.leftText: He has walled me in so I cannot escape; He has weighed me down with chains.
units.rightText: He hath walled me about, that I cannot go forth; he hath made my chain heavy.

units.leftText: Even when I cry out and plead for help, He shuts out my prayer.
units.rightText: Yea, when I cry, and call for help, he shutteth out my prayer.

units.leftText: He has barred my ways with cut stones; He has made my paths crooked.
units.rightText: He hath walled up my ways with hewn stone; he hath made my paths crooked.

units.leftText: He is a bear lying in wait, a lion hiding in ambush.
units.rightText: He is unto me as a bear lying in wait, as a lion in secret places.

units.leftText: He forced me off my path and tore me to pieces; He left me without help.
units.rightText: He hath turned aside my ways, and pulled me in pieces; he hath made me desolate.

units.leftText: He bent His bow and set me as the target for His arrow.
units.rightText: He hath bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.

units.leftText: He pierced my kidneys with His arrows.
units.rightText: He hath caused the shafts of his quiver to enter into my reins.

units.leftText: I am a laughingstock to all my people; they mock me in song all day long.
units.rightText: I am become a derision to all my people, and their song all the day.

units.leftText: He has filled me with bitterness; He has intoxicated me with wormwood.
units.rightText: He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath sated me with wormwood.

units.leftText: He has ground my teeth with gravel and trampled me in the dust.
units.rightText: He hath also broken my teeth with gravel stones; he hath covered me with ashes.

units.leftText: My soul has been deprived of peace; I have forgotten what prosperity is.
units.rightText: And thou hast removed my soul far off from peace; I forgat prosperity.

units.leftText: So I say, “My strength has perished, along with my hope from the LORD.” The Prophet’s Hope
units.rightText: And I said, My strength is perished, and mine expectation from Jehovah.

units.leftText: Remember my affliction and wandering, the wormwood and the gall.
units.rightText: Remember mine affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the gall.

units.leftText: Surely my soul remembers and is humbled within me.
units.rightText: My soul hath them still in remembrance, and is bowed down within me.

units.leftText: Yet I call this to mind, and therefore I have hope:
units.rightText: This I recall to my mind; therefore have I hope.

units.leftText: Because of the loving devotion of the LORD we are not consumed, for His mercies never fail.
units.rightText: It is of Jehovah’s lovingkindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
leftNotes: 3:22 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness!
units.rightText: They are new every morning; great is thy faithfulness.

units.leftText: “The LORD is my portion,” says my soul, “therefore I will hope in Him.”
units.rightText: Jehovah is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.

units.leftText: The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul who seeks Him.
units.rightText: Jehovah is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him.

units.leftText: It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD.
units.rightText: It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Jehovah.

units.leftText: It is good for a man to bear the yoke while he is still young.
units.rightText: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.

units.leftText: Let him sit alone in silence, for the LORD has laid it upon him.
units.rightText: Let him sit alone and keep silence, because he hath laid it upon him.

units.leftText: Let him bury his face in the dust— perhaps there is still hope.
units.rightText: Let him put his mouth in the dust, if so be there may be hope.

units.leftText: Let him offer his cheek to the one who would strike him; let him be filled with reproach.
units.rightText: Let him give his cheek to him that smiteth him; let him be filled full with reproach.

units.leftText: For the Lord will not cast us off forever.
units.rightText: For the Lord will not cast off for ever.

units.leftText: Even if He causes grief, He will show compassion according to His abundant loving devotion.
units.rightText: For though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his lovingkindnesses.

units.leftText: For He does not willingly afflict or grieve the sons of men.
units.rightText: For he doth not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men.

units.leftText: To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the land,
units.rightText: To crush under foot all the prisoners of the earth,

units.leftText: to deny a man justice before the Most High,
units.rightText: To turn aside the right of a man before the face of the Most High,

units.leftText: to subvert a man in his lawsuit— of these the Lord does not approve. God’s Justice
units.rightText: To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord approveth not.

units.leftText: Who has spoken and it came to pass, unless the Lord has ordained it?
units.rightText: Who is he that saith, and it cometh to pass, when the Lord commandeth it not?

units.leftText: Do not both adversity and good come from the mouth of the Most High?
units.rightText: Out of the mouth of the Most High cometh there not evil and good?

units.leftText: Why should any mortal man complain, in view of his sins?
units.rightText: Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?

units.leftText: Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the LORD.
units.rightText: Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to Jehovah.

units.leftText: Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God in heaven:
units.rightText: Let us lift up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens.

units.leftText: “We have sinned and rebelled; You have not forgiven.”
units.rightText: We have transgressed and have rebelled; thou hast not pardoned.

units.leftText: You have covered Yourself in anger and pursued us; You have killed without pity.
units.rightText: Thou hast covered with anger and pursued us; thou hast slain, thou hast not pitied.

units.leftText: You have covered Yourself with a cloud that no prayer can pass through.
units.rightText: Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through.

units.leftText: You have made us scum and refuse among the nations.
units.rightText: Thou hast made us an offscouring and refuse in the midst of the peoples.

units.leftText: All our enemies open their mouths against us.
units.rightText: All our enemies have opened their mouth wide against us.

units.leftText: Panic and pitfall have come upon us — devastation and destruction.
units.rightText: Fear and the pit are come upon us, devastation and destruction.

units.leftText: Streams of tears flow from my eyes over the destruction of the daughter of my people.
units.rightText: Mine eye runneth down with streams of water, for the destruction of the daughter of my people.

units.leftText: My eyes overflow unceasingly, without relief,
units.rightText: Mine eye poureth down, and ceaseth not, without any intermission,

units.leftText: until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.
units.rightText: Till Jehovah look down, and behold from heaven.

units.leftText: My eyes bring grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
units.rightText: Mine eye affecteth my soul, because of all the daughters of my city.

units.leftText: Without cause my enemies hunted me like a bird.
units.rightText: They have chased me sore like a bird, they that are mine enemies without cause.

units.leftText: They dropped me alive into a pit and cast stones upon me.
units.rightText: They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and have cast a stone upon me.

units.leftText: The waters flowed over my head, and I thought I was going to die.
units.rightText: Waters flowed over my head; I said, I am cut off.

units.leftText: I called on Your name, O LORD, out of the depths of the Pit.
units.rightText: I called upon thy name, O Jehovah, out of the lowest dungeon.

units.leftText: You heard my plea: “Do not ignore my cry for relief.”
units.rightText: Thou heardest my voice; hide not thine ear at my breathing, at my cry.

units.leftText: You drew near when I called on You; You said, “Do not be afraid.”
units.rightText: Thou drewest near in the day that I called upon thee; thou saidst, Fear not.

units.leftText: You defend my cause, O Lord; You redeem my life.
units.rightText: O Lord, thou hast pleaded the causes of my soul; thou hast redeemed my life.

units.leftText: You have seen, O LORD, the wrong done to me; vindicate my cause!
units.rightText: O Jehovah, thou hast seen my wrong; judge thou my cause.

units.leftText: You have seen all their malice, all their plots against me.
units.rightText: Thou hast seen all their vengeance and all their devices against me.

units.leftText: O LORD, You have heard their insults, all their plots against me —
units.rightText: Thou hast heard their reproach, O Jehovah, and all their devices against me,

units.leftText: the slander and murmuring of my assailants against me all day long.
units.rightText: The lips of those that rose up against me, and their device against me all the day.

units.leftText: When they sit and when they rise, see how they mock me in song.
units.rightText: Behold thou their sitting down, and their rising up; I am their song.

units.leftText: You will pay them back what they deserve, O LORD, according to the work of their hands.
units.rightText: Thou wilt render unto them a recompense, O Jehovah, according to the work of their hands.

units.leftText: Put a veil of anguish over their hearts; may Your curse be upon them!
units.rightText: Thou wilt give them hardness of heart, thy curse unto them.

units.leftText: You will pursue them in anger and exterminate them from under Your heavens, O LORD.
units.rightText: Thou wilt pursue them in anger, and destroy them from under the heavens of Jehovah.

units.leftText: How the gold has become tarnished, the pure gold has become dull! The gems of the temple lie scattered on every street corner.
units.rightText: How is the gold become dim! how is the most pure gold changed! The stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the head of every street.
leftNotes: 4:1 This chapter is an acrostic poem, each verse beginning with the successive letters of the Hebrew alphabet.

units.leftText: How the precious sons of Zion, once worth their weight in pure gold, are now esteemed as jars of clay, the work of a potter’s hands!
units.rightText: The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, How are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!

units.leftText: Even jackals offer their breasts to nurse their young, but the daughter of my people has become cruel, like an ostrich in the wilderness.
units.rightText: Even the jackals draw out the breast, they give suck to their young ones: The daughter of my people is become cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.

units.leftText: The nursing infant’s tongue clings in thirst to the roof of his mouth. Little children beg for bread, but no one gives them any.
units.rightText: The tongue of the sucking child cleaveth to the roof of his mouth for thirst: The young children ask bread, and no man breaketh it unto them.

units.leftText: Those who once ate delicacies are destitute in the streets; those brought up in crimson huddle in ash heaps.
units.rightText: They that did feed delicately are desolate in the streets: They that were brought up in scarlet embrace dunghills.

units.leftText: The punishment of the daughter of my people is greater than that of Sodom, which was overthrown in an instant without a hand turned to help her.
units.rightText: For the iniquity of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, That was overthrown as in a moment, and no hands were laid upon her.

units.leftText: Her dignitaries were brighter than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies were more ruddy than rubies, their appearance like sapphires.
units.rightText: Her nobles were purer than snow, they were whiter than milk; They were more ruddy in body than rubies, their polishing was as of sapphire.
leftNotes: 4:7 Or their polishing or their hair

units.leftText: But now their appearance is blacker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has shriveled on their bones; it has become as dry as a stick.
units.rightText: Their visage is blacker than a coal; they are not known in the streets: Their skin cleaveth to their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick.

units.leftText: Those slain by the sword are better off than those who die of hunger, who waste away, pierced with pain because the fields lack produce.
units.rightText: They that are slain with the sword are better than they that are slain with hunger; For these pine away, stricken through, for want of the fruits of the field.

units.leftText: The hands of compassionate women have cooked their own children, who became their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
units.rightText: The hands of the pitiful women have boiled their own children; They were their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.

units.leftText: The LORD has exhausted His wrath; He has poured out His fierce anger; He has kindled a fire in Zion, and it has consumed her foundations.
units.rightText: Jehovah hath accomplished his wrath, he hath poured out his fierce anger; And he hath kindled a fire in Zion, which hath devoured the foundations thereof.

units.leftText: The kings of the earth did not believe, nor any people of the world, that an enemy or a foe could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: The kings of the earth believed not, neither all the inhabitants of the world, That the adversary and the enemy would enter into the gates of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: But this was for the sins of her prophets and the guilt of her priests, who shed the blood of the righteous in her midst.
units.rightText: It is because of the sins of her prophets, and the iniquities of her priests, That have shed the blood of the just in the midst of her.

units.leftText: They wandered blind in the streets, defiled by this blood, so that no one dared to touch their garments.
units.rightText: They wander as blind men in the streets, they are polluted with blood, So that men cannot touch their garments.

units.leftText: “Go away! Unclean!” men shouted at them. “Away, away! Do not touch us!” So they fled and wandered. Among the nations it was said, “They can stay here no longer.”
units.rightText: Depart ye, they cried unto them, Unclean! depart, depart, touch not! When they fled away and wandered, men said among the nations, They shall no more sojourn here.

units.leftText: The presence of the LORD has scattered them; He regards them no more. The priests are shown no honor; the elders find no favor.
units.rightText: The anger of Jehovah hath scattered them; he will no more regard them: They respected not the persons of the priests, they favored not the elders.

units.leftText: All the while our eyes were failing as we looked in vain for help. We watched from our towers for a nation that could not save us.
units.rightText: Our eyes do yet fail in looking for our vain help: In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save.

units.leftText: They stalked our every step, so that we could not walk in our streets. Our end drew near, our time ran out, for our end had come!
units.rightText: They hunt our steps, so that we cannot go in our streets: Our end is near, our days are fulfilled; for our end is come.

units.leftText: Those who chased us were swifter than the eagles in the sky; they pursued us over the mountains and ambushed us in the wilderness.
units.rightText: Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the heavens: They chased us upon the mountains, they laid wait for us in the wilderness.

units.leftText: The LORD’s anointed, the breath of our life, was captured in their pits. We had said of him, “Under his shadow we will live among the nations.”
units.rightText: The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Jehovah, was taken in their pits; Of whom we said, Under his shadow we shall live among the nations.

units.leftText: So rejoice and be glad, O Daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz. Yet the cup will pass to you as well; you will get drunk and expose yourself.
units.rightText: Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of Uz: The cup shall pass through unto thee also; thou shalt be drunken, and shalt make thyself naked.

units.leftText: O Daughter of Zion, your punishment is complete; He will not prolong your exile. But He will punish your iniquity, O Daughter of Edom; He will expose your sins.
units.rightText: The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion; he will no more carry thee away into captivity: He will visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will uncover thy sins.
leftNotes: 4:22 Or He will not exile you again

units.leftText: Remember, O LORD, what has happened to us. Look and see our disgrace!
units.rightText: Remember, O Jehovah, what is come upon us: Behold, and see our reproach.

units.leftText: Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
units.rightText: Our inheritance is turned unto strangers, Our houses unto aliens.

units.leftText: We have become fatherless orphans; our mothers are widows.
units.rightText: We are orphans and fatherless; Our mothers are as widows.

units.leftText: We must buy the water we drink; our wood comes at a price.
units.rightText: We have drunken our water for money; Our wood is sold unto us.

units.leftText: We are closely pursued; we are weary and find no rest.
units.rightText: Our pursuers are upon our necks: We are weary, and have no rest.

units.leftText: We submitted to Egypt and Assyria to get enough bread.
units.rightText: We have given the hand to the Egyptians, And to the Assyrians, to be satisfied with bread.

units.leftText: Our fathers sinned and are no more, but we bear their punishment.
units.rightText: Our fathers sinned, and are not; And we have borne their iniquities.

units.leftText: Slaves rule over us; there is no one to deliver us from their hands.
units.rightText: Servants rule over us: There is none to deliver us out of their hand.

units.leftText: We get our bread at the risk of our lives because of the sword in the wilderness.
units.rightText: We get our bread at the peril of our lives, Because of the sword of the wilderness.

units.leftText: Our skin is as hot as an oven with fever from our hunger.
units.rightText: Our skin is black like an oven, Because of the burning heat of famine.

units.leftText: Women have been ravished in Zion, virgins in the cities of Judah.
units.rightText: They ravished the women in Zion, The virgins in the cities of Judah.

units.leftText: Princes have been hung up by their hands; elders receive no respect.
units.rightText: Princes were hanged up by their hand: The faces of elders were not honored.

units.leftText: Young men toil at millstones; boys stagger under loads of wood.
units.rightText: The young men bare the mill; And the children stumbled under the wood.

units.leftText: The elders have left the city gate; the young men have stopped their music.
units.rightText: The elders have ceased from the gate, The young men from their music.

units.leftText: Joy has left our hearts; our dancing has turned to mourning.
units.rightText: The joy of our heart is ceased; Our dance is turned into mourning.

units.leftText: The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
units.rightText: The crown is fallen from our head: Woe unto us! for we have sinned.

units.leftText: Because of this, our hearts are faint; because of these, our eyes grow dim—
units.rightText: For this our heart is faint; For these things our eyes are dim;

units.leftText: because of Mount Zion, which lies desolate, patrolled by foxes.
units.rightText: For the mountain of Zion, which is desolate: The foxes walk upon it.

units.leftText: You, O LORD, reign forever; Your throne endures from generation to generation.
units.rightText: Thou, O Jehovah, abidest for ever; Thy throne is from generation to generation.

units.leftText: Why have You forgotten us forever? Why have You forsaken us for so long?
units.rightText: Wherefore dost thou forget us for ever, And forsake us so long time?

units.leftText: Restore us to Yourself, O LORD, so we may return; renew our days as of old,
units.rightText: Turn thou us unto thee, O Jehovah, and we shall be turned; Renew our days as of old.

units.leftText: unless You have utterly rejected us and remain angry with us beyond measure.
units.rightText: But thou hast utterly rejected us; Thou art very wroth against us.
